limits: All fourteen follow-up runs are retained. Before preparation changes, the late-body trace failed at 152 ms Enter. After preparation changes, the late-body matrix run also failed at 152 ms Enter. The other twelve runs passed.
After the canonical formatting lookup change, all five final runs pass all nine historical phases. Maxima: module 104 ms, studio 120 ms, profiled studio 136 ms, late body 96 ms, footnote 144 ms.
Every completed workload passed text, formatting, surrounding-text, key-count and Enter-undo assertions. No application code changed within either five-run matrix.
Chrome traces are diagnostic and include script sampling, layout and GC instrumentation plus between-phase trace export. They are identified separately from the comparison matrix.

The original two 184 ms delays were not captured again; their exact causes remain unproven. Subsequent traces identified synchronous incoming-document setup and a 152 ms Enter response. No historical failures are discarded.

These are quantized Chrome Event Timing samples on one machine with a 16 ms reporting threshold. Key-to-rAF starts in the handler and excludes prior queuing. This is not population INP or an editor-wide latency guarantee.

The overlappingNativeCalls field is a diagnostic time-window intersection, not causal attribution. A quantized event duration can include a call that begins after the actual paint; do not attribute the whole call to that input response.

Native operations and background tasks may exceed 150 ms when no sampled input overlaps them. Full structural layout after Enter can still take seconds. Cold opening, exports, excluded native structures, compound edits and slower devices remain outside a 150 ms claim.
